gist: Manchester City's spending changed the football transfer market, raising prices globally.
Many clubs receiving money from City struggled to spend it effectively.
Some clubs not dealing with City directly also felt financial impacts via sell-on clauses.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Manchester City paid high fees and wages, shifting the transfer market. Clubs receiving large sums often struggled. Wolfsburg dropped in the Bundesliga after selling Kevin de Bruyne, and Monaco nearly faced relegation after selling Benjamin Mendy and Bernardo Silva. Arsenal did not challenge for the title during the period they sold four players to City. Meanwhile, ancillary fees from sell-on clauses benefited teams like Queens Park Rangers, Barnsley, and Wolves.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The influx of money was no guarantee of success, and rising prices affected others in the football economy. Clubs receiving cash sometimes floundered, while rivals not receiving funds may have been compromised.

gist: Mason Crane is recalled to England's squad for the Pakistan tri-series.
Jofra Archer is rested while Jos Buttler is out injured.
Uncapped pair James Coles and Henry Crocombe are included.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Mason Crane has been recalled for England's upcoming one-day international tri-series in Pakistan. Sam Curran and Adil Rashid return from injuries, while uncapped players James Coles and Henry Crocombe join the squad. Jofra Archer is rested, and Jos Buttler misses out due to a hamstring injury.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The series forms part of England's white-ball schedule as they build up to the 50-over World Cup. Crane also has an opportunity to push his case to be England's number one spinner in Test cricket.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: England will play in the tri-series in Pakistan, which also involves Sri Lanka, ahead of further fixtures in Australia and South Africa.

Rangers.standfirst: Amidst a raft of coaching changes in Scotland's youth set up, the under-21s delivered an eye-catching display, with Rangers winger Findlay Curtis at the heart of it.
